name: Trailing Digits Solver
description: A single Python 3.10+ module that solves the Trailing Digits problem. Reads b, d, a from stdin and outputs the maximum number of consecutive trailing digits d achievable in a bundle price k*b ≤ a. Uses an iterative approach incrementing n from 1 upward, checking modular congruence solvability via gcd and modular inverse at each step. Handles arbitrarily large a (up to 10^10000) using Python native big integers. Standard library only (~30-40 lines, single file with __main__ guard).

types.name: int
types.description: Python arbitrary-precision integer. All intermediate values (b, d, a, M, T_n, g, k0, answer) are ints. Python natively handles integers with thousands of digits.

types.name: str
types.description: Python string type, used for raw stdin line reading.

types.name: None
types.description: Python None type, used as return type for main() since it communicates via stdout.

types.name: ProblemInput

fields.name: b
fields.description: Bundle price — the base multiplier. Every candidate price is a positive multiple of b.

validators.error_message: b must be between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

fields.name: d
fields.description: Target trailing digit (0-9). We seek multiples of b whose trailing digits are all d.

validators.error_message: d must be a single digit between 0 and 9 inclusive.

fields.name: a
fields.description: Budget — maximum allowable value for k*b. Can be astronomically large (up to 10^10000). Must be read as Python int from string to preserve precision.

validators.error_message: a must have at most ~10001 digits (i.e., a <= 10^10000).

types.description: Parsed input for the Trailing Digits problem. Represents the three integers read from a single stdin line.

types.name: CongruenceResult
types.description: Outcome of attempting to solve the modular congruence k*b ≡ T_n (mod 10^n) for a given n.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Entry point. Reads one line from stdin containing three space-separated integers b, d, a. Computes and prints to stdout the maximum number of consecutive trailing digits d achievable in any positive multiple k*b where k*b ≤ a. Prints 0 if no multiple of b within budget ends in digit d. This function orchestrates parsing, the core algorithm loop, and output.

error_cases.name: malformed_input
error_cases.condition: stdin line does not contain exactly three space-separated integers

error_data.note: Per competitive programming convention, input is trusted to conform to constraints. No explicit error handling is implemented; Python will raise ValueError or IndexError naturally on malformed input.

error_cases.name: empty_stdin
error_cases.condition: stdin is empty or EOF reached before reading a line

error_data.note: Raised by input() if no data available on stdin.

preconditions: stdin contains exactly one line with three space-separated non-negative integers
postconditions: Exactly one line is printed to stdout containing a single non-negative integer
The printed integer n is the maximum value such that there exists a positive integer k where k*b <= a and the last n digits of k*b are all equal to d
If no positive multiple of b within budget [b, 2b, ..., floor(a/b)*b] has its last digit equal to d, the output is 0
Output is followed by a newline character (Python print default)

structured_side_effects.description: Reads exactly one line from standard input containing the problem parameters b, d, a.
Writes exactly one line to standard output containing the integer answer followed by a newline.

performance_budget.complexity: O(N^2) where N = number of digits of a (at most ~10000). Outer loop runs up to N iterations; each iteration performs big-integer arithmetic (gcd, modular inverse via pow) on numbers with up to N digits. Python big-int operations on N-digit numbers are O(N log N) or better with sub-quadratic multiplication, giving effective complexity around O(N^2 log N).

functions.name: parse_input
functions.description: Reads a single line from stdin and parses it into the three problem parameters b, d, a. Returns them as a ProblemInput struct. This is a logical sub-step of main(); in the actual single-file implementation it may be inlined, but the contract specifies it as a distinct logical function for clarity.

inputs.name: line
inputs.description: Raw input line from stdin, expected to contain exactly three space-separated non-negative integer tokens.

validators.expression: len(line.split()) == 3 and all(tok.isdigit() or (tok[0]=='-' and tok[1:].isdigit()) for tok in line.split())
validators.error_message: Input line must contain exactly three space-separated integers.

error_cases.name: wrong_token_count
error_cases.condition: line.split() does not yield exactly 3 tokens

error_data.detail: Expected exactly 3 space-separated integers on the input line.

error_cases.name: non_integer_token
error_cases.condition: Any of the three tokens cannot be parsed as a Python int

error_data.detail: All three tokens must be valid integer literals.

preconditions: line contains exactly three space-separated tokens that are valid integer representations
postconditions: All three fields are Python ints with correct values

performance_budget.complexity: O(N) where N is the number of digits in a (dominated by int() parsing of the large integer a).

functions.name: solve
functions.description: Core algorithm. Given b, d, a, computes the maximum number of consecutive trailing digits d achievable in any positive multiple k*b ≤ a. Iterates n from 1 upward (up to len(str(a)) digits), maintaining M=10^n and T_n incrementally. For each n: computes g=gcd(b, M), checks if T_n is divisible by g (solvability condition), reduces the congruence to find the smallest positive k via modular inverse pow(b', -1, M'), and verifies k*b ≤ a. Tracks and returns the maximum achievable n.

inputs.name: a
inputs.description: Budget upper bound. 1 <= a. Can be up to 10^10000.

error_cases.name: modular_inverse_does_not_exist
error_cases.condition: gcd(b // g, M // g) != 1 after reduction — this should never happen because g = gcd(b, M) ensures the reduced values are coprime, but is listed for completeness

error_data.detail: Internal error: reduced b' and M' are not coprime. This indicates a bug in the gcd reduction step.

preconditions: a >= b (implicitly required for any solution to exist with k >= 1; if a < b, answer is 0)
postconditions: Returned value n satisfies 0 <= n <= len(str(a))
If n > 0, there exists a positive integer k such that k*b <= a and (k*b) mod 10^n == d * (10^n - 1) / 9 (i.e., last n digits are all d)
For all m where n < m <= len(str(a)), no positive integer k exists such that k*b <= a and (k*b) mod 10^m == d * (10^m - 1) / 9
If n == 0, no positive multiple of b within [1, a] has its units digit equal to d
Special case: when d == 0, T_n == 0 for all n, meaning we seek k*b divisible by 10^n

performance_budget.complexity: O(N^2) where N = len(str(a)). Loop runs at most N iterations. Each iteration: gcd on (b, 10^n) is O(n * log(b)) ≈ O(n); modular inverse via pow(b', -1, M') on n-digit modulus is O(n * M(n)) where M(n) is multiplication cost; comparison k0*b <= a is O(n). Dominant cost is modular inverse computation across all iterations.

invariants: M is always equal to 10^n at the start of each loop iteration for the current n
T_n is always equal to d * (10^n - 1) / 9, i.e., n repetitions of digit d (e.g., d=4, n=3 → T_n=444); when d=0, T_n=0 for all n
T_n is maintained incrementally: T_{n+1} = T_n + d * 10^n (equivalently, T is updated as T += d * prev_power where prev_power tracks 10^(n-1))
M is maintained incrementally: M_{n+1} = M_n * 10
The answer variable is monotonically non-decreasing during the loop (once n is achievable, all smaller values remain achievable, though the answer only tracks the maximum)
g = gcd(b, M) divides both b and M, ensuring the reduced congruence b'*k ≡ T' (mod M') has gcd(b', M') = 1, guaranteeing the modular inverse exists when T_n % g == 0
k0 is always the smallest positive integer satisfying k*b ≡ T_n (mod M), so k0*b is the smallest positive multiple of b with the desired n trailing digits
All intermediate values are Python ints — no floating point is ever used
The loop terminates after at most len(str(a)) iterations because n cannot exceed the total number of digits in a (k*b <= a implies k*b has at most len(str(a)) digits)
The program uses only Python standard library (math.gcd, built-in pow with three arguments for modular inverse)
